module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 447

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/447](https://www.erdosproblems.com/447)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Kl71] Kleitman, Daniel, *Collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union*.
  Proceedings of the LA Meeting AMS (1971), 153-155.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos447

/-- The largest size of a union-free collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$. -/
noncomputable def maxUnionFree (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup { k | ∃ F : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), F.UnionFree ∧ F.card = k }

/--
How large can a union-free collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ be? By union-free we mean
there are no solutions to $A\cup B=C$ with distinct $A,B,C\in \mathcal{F}$. Must
$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert =o(2^n)$?

In [Er65b] Erdős reported that the estimate $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=o(2^n)$ was proved in
unpublished work by Sárközy and Szemerédi.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_447.parts.i : answer(True) ↔
    (fun n : ℕ => (maxUnionFree n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n) := by
  sorry

/--
How large can a union-free collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ be? By union-free we mean
there are no solutions to $A\cup B=C$ with distinct $A,B,C\in \mathcal{F}$. Perhaps even
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert <(1+o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}?$$

Solved by Kleitman [Kl71], who proved
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert <(1+o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos447.lean"]
theorem erdos_447.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ, (c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (maxUnionFree n : ℝ) < (1 + c n) * (n.choose (n / 2) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos447

reformulations.difference: The source's '|F| < (1+o(1)) C(n, floor(n/2))' for every union-free family F is stated about `maxUnionFree n`, an sSup over ℕ of the sizes of union-free families. It reads: there is c : ℕ → ℝ with c =o[atTop] 1 such that eventually (∀ᶠ) maxUnionFree n < (1 + c n) * n.choose (n / 2), with a strict inequality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: 1. The sSup set is non-empty (the empty family) and bounded above by 2^n, so maxUnionFree n is the attained maximum (proved via Nat.sSup_mem). A bound for every family is therefore the same as a bound for the maximum. 2. The ∃c/∀ᶠ/strict form is equivalent to '∀ ε>0, eventually maxUnionFree n ≤ (1+ε)·C(n,⌊n/2⌋)' (proved in Lean). Strictness and 'eventually' are absorbed by the freedom in c, e.g. by adding 1/(n+1). 3. The middle layer is union-free, so C(n,⌊n/2⌋) ≤ maxUnionFree n (proved). Hence the right-hand side is also equivalent to maxUnionFree n ~ C(n,⌊n/2⌋) (proved in Lean), which is Kleitman's theorem as stated in Balogh–Wagner.

review.notes:
No misformalizations found; all three declarations match erdosproblems.com/447 and its status "PROVED (LEAN)".

Lean checks (scratch files in /workspace/review):
- `maxUnionFree n` is an attained maximum, with C(n,⌊n/2⌋) ≤ maxUnionFree n ≤ 2^n (lower bound from the middle layer).
- Brute-force values for n = 0..3 are 1, 2, 3, 5. These exceed C(n,⌊n/2⌋), so the eventual (∀ᶠ) form in part ii is needed, and the file uses it.
- The right-hand side of parts.ii is equivalent to maxUnionFree n ~ C(n,⌊n/2⌋).
- The right-hand side of parts.ii implies that of parts.i. The proof uses the elementary bound centralBinom(m)^2·(3m+1) ≤ 16^m.

formal_proof link:
- The cited v4.29.1 file has no sorry or custom axioms. It does not build under the sandbox's Lean v4.33.1 (aesop failures from version drift).
- The same author's v4.33.0 copy has identical UnionFree and MaxUnionFree definitions and the same theorem `erdos_447 : MaxUnionFree ~ C(n, n/2)`. It builds cleanly here with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
- I compiled it to an olean, proved its MaxUnionFree equals the file's maxUnionFree, and derived `type_of% Erdos447.erdos_447.parts.ii` and `type_of% Erdos447.erdos_447.parts.i` from it, with only the standard axioms.
- The automation in that proof is fragile: renaming its namespace, or importing the FC module into the same file, breaks one of its tactic blocks. Unrelated to the statements.

Attribution nuance (not reported as a finding):
- The part ii docstring follows erdosproblems.com in crediting the (1+o(1)) bound to Kleitman 1971 [Kl71].
- Balogh–Wagner (arXiv:1601.03659) say Kleitman first proved 2√2·C(n,n/2) and later (1+o(1))·C(n,n/2), citing his 1976 JCTA paper "Extremal properties of collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union". Sudakov–Tomon–Wagner also cite the 1976 paper.
- Fox–Lee–Sudakov (arXiv:1012.3127) credit the stronger bound (1+c/√n)·C(n,⌊n/2⌋) to the 1971 PSPUM paper.
- The docstring is therefore defensible. Maintainers could optionally cite the 1976 paper as well.
